exposure: causes of ICU admission (hemorrhage, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, amniotic fluid embolism, cardiovascular disease, cerebrovascular disease, infection, pulmonary disease, trauma, suicide)
interventions (blood transfusions, mechanical ventilation, transcatheter arterial embolization)
outcome: clinical presentation and outcomes differences between survivors and non-survivors
cohort: The study included 8,184 obstetric patients from 195 institutions in Japan who were admitted to the ICU and delivered either during hospitalization or within one week prior to admission.
finding: Hemorrhage was identified as the primary cause of obstetric ICU admissions in Japan, with an overall in-hospital mortality rate of 1.1%.
